name: Common evening-primrose
grown_as: A wild flower of the wildlife fringe, a biennial: a rosette in the first year, a tall flowering stem in the second.
habit: First year: a flat rosette 20 to 30 cm across. Second year: a stiff upright stem 0.5 to 1.5 m, usually unbranched or with a few side branches, leafy all the way up to a leafy flower spike at the top.

leaf.arrangement: A rosette at the base, then alternate and crowded up the stem
leaf.outline: Lance-shaped to narrowly oval, 5 to 15 cm on the stem, up to 20 cm in the rosette
leaf.margin: A few small, widely spaced teeth or almost smooth, often a little wavy
leaf.veins: A broad pale midrib, often pink or red, with fine side veins curving forward
leaf.stalk: Rosette leaves on short stalks; stem leaves almost stalkless
leaf.colour: Mid green, the midrib pale or red; rosettes often red-tinged in winter

flower.form: An open shallow cup to flat flower, opening in the evening and fading by the next afternoon
flower.petals: Four, free, broad, overlapping, each wider than long with a shallow notch at the tip, so the flower looks almost square
flower.centre: Eight yellow stamens around a stigma split into four arms in an X
flower.behind: Four green sepals, folded right back down against the long, slender green flower tube (3 to 4 cm) that looks like a stalk
flower.carried: In a leafy spike at the top of the stem, a few opening at a time, facing up and out, with buds above and young pods below

fruit: Long narrow pods 2 to 3.5 cm, four-angled, held stiffly upright and pressed close to the stem all down the old spike; green, ripening brown and splitting at the top into four. Seeds tiny (1 to 2 mm), angular and irregular, reddish brown.
seedling: Two small round-oval seed leaves on stalks, then narrow oval true leaves with a pale midrib, making a flat rosette
winter: The first-year rosette stays flat and green, often flushed red, through winter. Dead brown seed stems stand into winter with their split pods.

leaf: lance-shaped leaf with a broad pale or reddish midrib
few small distant teeth or none
bloom: four broad notched yellow petals, flower looking almost square
an X-shaped four-armed stigma in the middle
green sepals folded back down a long slender tube
seedling: first true leaves narrow with a pale midrib
young: a flat rosette of lance-shaped leaves with pale midribs, no stem
flower: pale yellow four-petalled flowers at the top of a leafy spike
upright narrow pods already forming below the flowers
seedhead: a tall brown stem lined with long, narrow, upright pods pressed to it
pods split into four at the tips

look_alikes: Large-flowered evening-primrose (Oenothera glazioviana), the commonest one in Britain, has bigger flowers (6 to 10 cm), red-striped sepals and red-based hairs on the stem. Small-flowered evening-primrose (O. cambrica) has smaller flowers and red-striped sepals. Rosettes can be confused with foxglove (softer, scalloped) or great willowherb.
